transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Head of ML, Tempest), Ravi Singh (Eng Manager), Lena Ortiz (CTO)

--- Auto Summary (optional):
Redwood quickstart, free credits, hosted vs dedicated, private/VPC questions, benchmarks, next steps to kick off trial and benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Samir our solutions engineer. You all good on audio?
[00:07] Maya: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Jordan. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:11] Jordan: Of course. Quick agenda, I want to understand your goals, show how the PLG quickstart works, talk free credits/time-to-first-token, and then Samir can answer infra questions - hosted, dedicated, private. Sound good?
[00:20] Ravi: Yup, that's perfect. Our main ask: we want to get a small proof of concept live in 2 weeks and validate latency and token cost estimates.
[00:28] Jordan: Great. Can you give a quick overview of Tempest's current stack and who will own the evaluation?
[00:33] Maya: Sure. We're a mid-stage analytics platform. Our model inference is currently split - some in-house smaller models, and we use a managed endpoint from another vendor for larger LLM tasks. Our infra is AWS, we use EKS and have a VPC. Ravi will own the implementation, I own the success criteria. Lena is overseeing compliance and vendor decisions.
[00:50] Samir: Quick clarifying Q - when you say "larger LLM tasks" are those real-time chat features or batch embedding jobs?
[00:55] Maya: Both, actually. We have a chat assistant in our product and nightly embedding pipelines for search reindexing. Latency matters for the chat, cost matters for the nightly jobs.
[01:06] Samir: Got it. For the PLG quickstart our hosted API gets you to first token in minutes, we also provide free credits to run small-scale benchmarks. Dedicated is more for sustained predictable throughput; private/VPC is for strict data residency and network isolation.
[01:20] Lena: Two compliance questions up front - do you have SOC 2, and can we integrate with our KMS? Also need audit logs.
[01:27] Jordan: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II and we support KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. Audit logs and request tracing are available through the console; we'll share the SOC2 pack and security docs after the call.
[01:37] Ravi: Cool. On the hosted path - what kind of latency can we expect for a mid-sized model? We're doing 800-1k token responses with a 50-100ms per-token budget ideally.
[01:46] Samir: On hosted, runway depends on model and sequence length. For our verified LLMs we typically see 15-25 ms per token on gX-class hardware for streaming generation at a 512 context. For 800-1k tokens you'll want to look at throughput vs tail latency; we can tune batching and KV cache to keep user-facing 95th percentile under your SLO.
[02:06] Maya: Are those numbers for your default hosted model or a quantized variant?
[02:09] Samir: That's for our curated models on optimised infra. Quantized models reduce GPU memory and cost, sometimes adding a slight tail increase. We'll provide model profiles in the docs.
[02:18] Jordan: For time-to-first-token, most teams sign up, grab the API key, and run a hello prompt in under 10 minutes - that's the PLG quickstart. We give $1k in free credits for initial testing, that usually covers a few thousand queries depending on model.
[02:29] Ravi: Nice. How do you handle rate limits and quotas during an eval? We don't want noisy throttling while testing.
[02:34] Jordan: During trials we provision a temporary uplift to avoid noisy throttling for the benchmark window; Samir can configure concurrency buckets.
[02:41] Samir: Yep, we can set a higher concurrency for the pilot and monitor the metrics. Also we can run a small benchmark job from our side to mimic your traffic shape.
[02:48] Maya: On the dedicated option - what's the commit/contract like? And how long to provision?
[02:52] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity; typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on region and GPU availability. Contracts are monthly or annual commitments. You get predictable throughput and data isolation.
[03:02] Lena: For private/VPC do you still manage the control plane? We're a little wary of vendor-managed control planes in our VPC.
[03:08] Jordan: For Private we offer a customer-managed networking option - the control plane can be run in your VPC and we support an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. We'll share the deployment options doc.
[03:17] Ravi: Ok. On security: does the hosted flow retain any customer data for model tuning? We need to be explicit about retention and whether training data could see customer text.
[03:25] Samir: By default hosted logs are retained for a short period for observability; we have retention controls and can disable retention for sensitive customers. Training on customer data is not done without explicit opt-in. We'll include the data retention policy in the security pack.
[03:37] Maya: Great. Can you demo the quickstart flow briefly? Just to confirm it's self-serve.
[03:41] Jordan: Sure - high level: sign up, create API key, call /v1/generate with a simple prompt or use SDKs. I'll walk through the console in 2 mins.
[03:49] [Jordan screenshares - brief pause while he navigates]
[03:59] Jordan: Ok, here is the console, quickstart doc link in the top-right, you can request free credits from billing, and the SDK snippet is copy-paste. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'... it's literally a few lines.
[04:19] Ravi: That looks nice. Any SDKs for Python/Node?
[04:22] Jordan: Yes both, plus Go. We'll send code samples in the email.
[04:25] Maya: About the free credits - is that applied automatically when I sign up or do you provision after we ask?
[04:30] Jordan: For initial accounts it's automatic up to a baseline, but for larger trial budgets we manually provision. For your benchmark we'll do the manual uplift.
[04:37] Samir: One note on benchmarking: please share your request distribution - average tokens, concurrency, and QPS. We can then provision a realistic test and estimate costs for hosted vs dedicated.
[04:47] Maya: We'll share that. Our chat uses short prompts but sometimes gets long contexts, and embeddings job is heavy in tokens but batched overnight.
[04:55] Lena: Another question - do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for enterprise teams?
[05:00] Jordan: Yes, SAML SSO, RBAC, SCIM, and IP allowlists for private deployments. Those are in our enterprise pack.
[05:07] Ravi: For the embedding job - if we run 10M tokens nightly, how do you recommend we reduce cost? Is batching or quantization more effective?
[05:15] Samir: For large batch workloads quantization + offline batching + caching (where applicable) yields the best unit economics. Also routing embeddings to cheaper quantized model variants works well. Redwood Optimize will suggest profiles.
[05:26] Maya: Do you have any case studies for companies with similar workflows?
[05:29] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a benchmark vs cost spreadsheet from Aura Labs who moved embeddings to Redwood Dedicated and saw 40% cost reduction.
[05:36] [06:00 timestamp jump in transcript to simulate longer call continuation]
[06:00] Samir: Quick note about tail latency, we can set per-request priority to avoid cold-starts for your high-SLO traffic. There's also KV cache warmers for chat history.
[06:10] Ravi: Sounds useful. How invasive is the integration with our EKS setup if we go Private?
[06:15] Samir: The private agent runs as a set of managed services inside your VPC; it's containerized and can be run on EKS. We provide helm charts and recommend an HA control-plane with 3 replicas. There's some initial network setup with ingress and egress rules.
[06:29] Maya: For the trial can we start hosted and then move to dedicated or private if things look good?
[06:34] Jordan: Absolutely, the API surface is the same. You can pin model versions and rollout policies when moving. We also support canary rollouts between hosted and dedicated variants.
[06:44] Lena: On compliance timeline - if we need an internal security review, how fast can you provide the SOC2 packet and architecture diagrams?
[06:51] Jordan: We'll send the SOC2 pack and architecture diagrams within 24 hours after this call. Also we can set up a security deep dive with our security engineering team next week if desired.
[06:59] Maya: That would be helpful. Also, we want to know cost at scale - like ballpark numbers for 10M tokens/month on hosted vs dedicated commit.
[07:07] Samir: We'll run a cost model once you give us the token mix. Hosted keeps you flexible but higher per-token; dedicated pushes unit cost down with commit. We'll produce a model in the benchmark deliverable.
[07:18] Ravi: One last technical - do you expose per-token traces in the console for debugging generation issues?
[07:22] Samir: Yes, token-level latency breakdowns, per-route traces, and a replay for failed requests. There's also payload logging with redaction options.
[07:31] Jordan: Okay folks, to recap: Jordan sends quickstart + free credits link and SOC2/security docs by tomorrow. Samir will prepare benchmark config and cost estimate after Tempest shares request distribution. Tempest will provision an eval team and deliver workload profile by Monday. We'll schedule a benchmarking run and a security deep dive.
[07:50] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone. Really keen to see time-to-first-token.
[07:55] Ravi: Thanks. We'll get that workload sheet over.
[07:58] Lena: Thanks, Jordan and Samir.
[08:00] Jordan: Great - talk soon. Bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional overlaps and small mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cache" was sometimes captured as "K V cash") and product names like "Redwood Optimize" occasionally split. There are pauses during the screen-share portion.
